You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual-ARC pattern notes

## Reflection tiling from demonstrations
Observed rule: transform an H×W grid into a 3H×2W grid by reflection tiling. The output has three vertical bands and two horizontal blocks:
- Vertical bands, from top to bottom: vertically flipped input, input, vertically flipped input.
- Horizontal blocks, left to right: horizontally flipped version of the current band, then the unflipped current band.
- Equivalently each cell in a tile is transformed by independent row/column reflection according to tile position. This yields 3×2 reflected tiles and preserves all colors.

Evidence from task-7d545d26: 9×1 input became 27×2 with vertical orientations reverse/original/reverse and each row duplicated horizontally; 1×15 input became 3×30 with each row equal to reversed sequence followed by original. Applying this to a 5×10 test produced the correct output (15×20).

When seeing similar demo geometry, identify output dimensions as multiples of input dimensions, then compare tile ordering and reflections. This task family may recur with new input shapes/data; request demos only if the reflection/tiling orientation is ambiguous.

## Fill hollow rectangular frames by interior-area parity
Observed task rule: find monochrome, axis-aligned hollow rectangular frames (including sizes >3x3) and fill their entire enclosed interior, preserving the frame. Fill with color 2 when the number of interior cells is even, and color 7 when the number of interior cells is odd. Leave background and non-frame cells unchanged. Equivalently, for a rectangular frame with interior dimensions h×w, use 2 if h*w is even, otherwise 7.

Evidence: Demo 1 showed 4×4 frames (2×2=4 interior cells) filled with 2 and a 3×3 frame (1 interior cell) filled with 7. Demo 2 showed 6×6 frame with 4×4 interior filled 2; 4×4 frames with 2×2 interiors filled 2; 7×7 frame with 5×5 interior filled 7; and a 3×3 frame with 1×1 interior filled 7. Applied to task-e157ad0f: 4×4 (2×2 interior) frames filled 2, 5×5 (3×3 interior) frames filled 7; submission was confirmed correct. For future instances, request a demonstration if the palette/rule has not been established; otherwise compute the area parity and submit the grid with only frame interiors changed.

## Separator-grid tally encoding (task-e0d54f2b)
Observed a grid partitioned by full-color separator rows/columns into equal rectangular tiles. Produce one output cell per tile, keeping tile order (top-to-bottom, left-to-right). In each tile, count the single non-background/non-separator marker color. In all three examples, tiles contained either one or two markers: a tile with two markers maps to output color 1; a tile with one marker maps to the other output color used by the task (demo 1: 3; demo 2: 5; solved test: 4). The output's alternate color is therefore task/palette-specific; infer it from examples and do not assume it is always the same. Preserve the tile layout; separators are excluded.

Evidence: Demo 1 (15×11) separators were color 6, marker 7, background 3; 4×3 tiles of size 3×3. Its output was [[1,1,1],[1,3,3],[3,3,1],[3,1,1]], agreeing with 2 markers→1 and 1 marker→3. Demo 2 (14×24) separators 4, marker 9, background 5; 5×5 tiles of size 2×4. Output had 1s except one-marker tiles at (row 2,col 2) and (row 5,col 2), which were 5. Test for task-e0d54f2b (14×15) separators 6, marker 8, background 4; 3×4 tiles of size 4×3. Correct submission was [[1,1,1,1],[1,4,1,1],[1,1,4,1]]. The two tiles with one 8 became 4; all tiles with two 8s became 1. Submission was confirmed correct after one incorrect submission; don't infer the rule from the mistaken earlier grid.

For future instances: identify separator color and equal tile bounds first, count markers in every tile, build an output grid with matching tile arrangement, map one-marker tiles to the demonstrated alternate color and two-marker tiles to 1, then verify every tile count and output dimension before submitting. Request a demo if the mapping or marker-count cases are not established; avoid unnecessary requests once clear.

## Recolor full monochrome separator lines (task-fcbeee9f)
Observed rule: find any row or column whose every cell is the same color, and recolor the entire line to 2. Keep all other cells unchanged. If multiple such lines exist, recolor each; intersections naturally become 2. In the demo, all-4 rows and columns became 2 (including the solid full-width rows and solid full-height columns), while partial 4s and other colors stayed unchanged. In the test, the all-8 first column and all-8 rows 3 and 15 became 2; all other 8/3 cells remained as-is. Submission confirmed correct with zero wrong attempts.

For future instances, identify the repeated/background color and scan the original grid for complete monochrome rows and columns; recolor each such complete line to 2 simultaneously. Do not recolor partial patterns or infer separators from near-complete lines. Preserve dimensions and verify line intersections.

# Continual-ARC pattern note: binary mask intersection

Observed one ARC task with a vertical composite row layout: each row contained a left binary pattern, a one-cell separator column, and a right binary mask of matching width. The left pattern used 0 and 3; separator was 1; the right mask used 0 and 3. Rule inferred and verified: retain the left-pattern 3 only where the corresponding right-mask cell is also 3, and render the retained cells as 2; all other output cells are 0. Output has the shared panel dimensions (separator and mask are not included).

Demo variant used a horizontal separator: top binary image, separator row of 4s, then a mostly-1 mask with one 0. Output preserved top-image 1s only where mask was 1, recolored to 2; zeros remained 0. General rule: elementwise AND/intersection of the two binary panels, then encode foreground as 2 and background as 0. Determine orientation and separator from the grid; panels are corresponding same-sized regions.

Solved from two demonstrations. Likely task rule: the input contains solid, axis-aligned monochrome rectangular objects on a uniform background, with occasional single-cell color corruption inside rectangles and scattered single-cell noise outside. Reconstruct each rectangle as a fully filled rectangle in its original dominant color; remove isolated external noise by restoring the background. Preserve all genuine rectangles, including rectangles of different colors—do not erase a color just because it appears unusual or matches a corruption color.

Evidence:
- Demo 1: background 9; two color-5 rectangles (rows 0–3, cols 1–3; rows 6–9, cols 3–7). Interior stray colors were restored to 5; isolated exterior speckles were replaced with 9.
- Demo 2: background 6; multiple rectangles of colors 5, 7, 3, and 0. Interior stray cells were repaired to their rectangle's color; exterior speckles removed. Distinct rectangles all retained.
- Solved test: background 2; retain/fill rectangles of 8 and 9. In particular preserve 9 blocks near top and lower-left, repair the anomalous 5 in the 3x3 8-block (to 8), repair 0 in the 9 rectangle (to 9), and remove outside isolated 0/5/6/1 cells to background 2.

Practical approach: identify fully filled rectangular blocks by their bounding boxes and dominant color; correct deviations within those bounds; set remaining isolated non-background pixels outside blocks back to background. A true rectangle may have isolated noise immediately adjacent but still be independently identifiable. Verify every input rectangle is retained, including multi-color rectangle sets.
